home.tabs_lead: Three tabs instead of four apps. What waits on you, what you wait on, and what you chose to see again later.

tabs.name: My turn
tabs.text: Someone is waiting on you: a reply, a review, a fix, a task, a reminder.

tabs.name: Waiting
tabs.text: You’re waiting on others. Remora suggests reviewers and drafts the nudge.

tabs.name: Snoozed
tabs.text: Out of sight until it’s time, or until there’s news. With a reason.

home.verbs_lead: A Slack question and a GitLab comment both land in To reply. Messages are sorted on your computer with keyword rules, plus Apple’s on-device language model on the Mac. No generative AI, nothing sent. React ✅ in Slack and the item moves to Done.
home.verbs_more: To read and Waiting are shown, never counted: the badge only counts what needs you.
home.line_title: Cast a reminder from the menu bar.
home.line_lead: Grab the fish and pull down. The further you drag, the later it comes back: minutes, then hours, then days. Release, type what to remember, press Enter. Esc cancels.
home.line_more: Or press + in the inbox; on Windows, Ctrl+Alt+R from anywhere. Due reminders arrive as notifications, with Snooze buttons.
home.features_lead: Every feature has one job: fewer things on your mind at once.

features.title: Done until it changes
features.body: Mark it done and it stays gone, until a new commit, an approval or a reply brings it back.

features.title: Snooze with a reason
features.body: Waiting for someone, no time now, needs focus. Each reason picks a sensible return time, and “until there’s news” is one of them.

features.title: Review prep
features.body: “~6 min · 4 files · tests ✓ · Auth” under each review request, from file paths and line counts only. Then a session, quick wins first.

features.title: Waiting assistant
features.body: No reviewer on your merge request? Suggestions from who usually reviews there. Silent for a day? A drafted nudge, which you copy. Remora never sends.

features.title: Notifications that act
features.body: Approved, changes requested, checks failed, a reminder due. On the Mac, mark it done or snooze it right from the notification; on Windows, a click opens it.

features.title: Learns your habits
features.body: What you handle fast and what you push back, learned on your computer. It breaks ties, and a small star says why.

home.sources_lead: Connect as many accounts as you need and name them: “Work GitLab”, “Client Slack”. Each one opens in its own app when it’s installed.

home.why_title: Why not just use what you have?
home.why_lead: Fair question: your tools already have inboxes. Here is what changes when they become one.

why.title: Each tool’s own inbox
why.body: GitHub notifications, Linear’s inbox, Jira: each is the best place to act on its own items, and each has its own badge to check. Remora lists what needs you from all of them, then opens each item in its tool.

why.title: Slack’s Later
why.body: Good for messages you chose to keep. It only holds Slack, and only what you saved by hand. Remora picks up mentions and direct messages itself, and files the question under To reply, next to the review waiting on you.

why.title: A menu bar app for code reviews
why.body: gitbar, which inspired Remora, keeps your merge requests in the menu bar, and does it well. Remora keeps the idea for every tool you connect, and sorts by verb: To review, To reply, To fix.

why.title: A hosted unified inbox
why.body: It follows you on every device, which Remora doesn’t. But your tokens and messages go through its servers. Remora has no server: it talks to each tool from your computer, and sorts there.

home.privacy_lead: No data leaves your computer except to the tools you allow. Enforced in code, checked by tests, lockable by your IT.

privacy.title: Only allowed destinations
privacy.body: Each tool declares the hosts it may reach. Any other address is blocked, look-alike domains included.

privacy.title: External AI off by default
privacy.body: The assistant is opt-in. Your organization can forbid it, and then every AI feature disappears.

privacy.title: Managed by your IT
privacy.body: Allowed tools, AI and avatars can be locked with a configuration profile (MDM). Group Policy on Windows.

home.privacy_more: Every data flow, and how it is enforced

faq.question: Is my data sent to a Remora server?
faq.answer: There is no Remora server. The app talks directly to the tools you connect, keeps its data in your user folder and your tokens in the macOS Keychain or the Windows Credential Manager. No telemetry, no analytics, no crash reports.

faq.question: Do I need an AI assistant?
faq.answer: No. Sorting, ranking, snooze advice and review prep all run on your computer without generative AI. The assistant (Claude or an OpenAI-compatible model) only adds optional briefs and summaries, and it is off until you, and your organization, allow it.

faq.question: Can my AI agent use Remora?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and other agents that speak MCP can ask Remora what waits on you, list a tab or add a reminder, through remora mcp on your computer. They never get your tokens, and they can’t write to your tools. Your organization can turn it off. Remora and your agents.

faq.question: Does it work with GitHub Enterprise and self-hosted GitLab?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter your host when you connect the account; Remora only talks to that host. Setup for each tool: connecting your tools.

faq.question: Is there a Windows version?
faq.answer: Yes, in preview: Remora-Setup.exe for Windows 10 or 11, installed for your user only (no admin rights). Same rules, the same tools and the same assistant (Claude or OpenAI-compatible), same compliance model, with the policy in the registry for Group Policy or Intune. It sorts messages with keywords only. The installer isn’t signed yet: if SmartScreen warns, click More info → Run anyway.

faq.question: Is there a Linux version?
faq.answer: Yes, in preview and community supported: Remora-x86_64.AppImage, which updates itself, or Remora-amd64.deb for Ubuntu and Debian. The same app as on Windows, with the policy in /etc/remora/policy.json. It needs WebKitGTK 4.1, a keyring (GNOME Keyring, KWallet or KeePassXC) and a tray, or it opens as a window. Getting started on Linux.

faq.question: Why does macOS ask for my Keychain password?
faq.answer: Remora keeps all your tokens in one Keychain item. macOS asks once per new build of an app that isn’t signed by a registered developer. Choose Always Allow.

faq.question: macOS says it can’t check the app?
faq.answer: Remora isn’t notarized yet. Right-click it and choose Open; on macOS 15, use System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. macOS only asks once.

faq.question: How much does it cost?
faq.answer: Nothing. Remora is free software under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence, and its source code is on GitHub, so your security team can read exactly what it does.

home.final_lead: Connect one tool, see what needs you, close the other tabs.

features.title: One inbox, built to calm down.
features.lead: Everything Remora does, grouped by the moment you need it.

groups.name: The inbox
groups.intro: Sorted by what to do, never more than you can take in.

items.title: My turn and Waiting
items.body: My turn holds what someone waits on you for. Waiting holds what you wait on others for. Snoozed and Done are one click away.

items.title: Verbs
items.body: To reply, To review, To fix, Ready to merge, To do, Reminders, To read, Waiting on others. Messages are classified on your computer, in English and French; when unsure, To reply.

items.title: Done
items.body: Hides an item until something changes on it. Clear the Done list in one click; cleared items still come back on new activity.

items.title: Pin
items.body: Keeps an item at the top, whatever arrives next.

items.title: Priority, then habits
items.body: Overdue and due today first, then the tool’s priority (Linear Urgent, High…), the nearest due date, recent activity. Low priority is shown, never counted.

items.title: Five at a time
items.body: Long bundles show their top five and “Show N more”. A smart summary of the rest when the assistant is allowed.

groups.name: The menu bar and the tray
groups.intro: Remora lives in the Mac’s menu bar or the Windows system tray: no window to keep open.

items.title: One count per tool
items.body: The fish and a single number, or on the Mac one count per tool, ordered by the most pressing verb. Start a task and it shows alone, with how long you’ve been on it.

items.title: Drag to remind
items.body: Pull the fish down to cast a reminder; a bubble shows when it comes back. Further down means later. On Windows, Ctrl+Alt+R. Repeat it every day, weekday or week.

items.title: Gestures
items.body: Two fingers on the trackpad: right to mark done, left to snooze. On Windows, buttons on each row.

items.title: Opens in the right app
items.body: Slack and Linear items open in their desktop app when it’s installed (⌥-click, or Shift-click on Windows, for the web), with the browser as fallback.

groups.name: Time
groups.intro: Snooze is a decision, so Remora helps you make a good one.

items.title: Snooze or remind
items.body: Hide an item until later, or keep it visible and get a reminder. Presets (later today, this evening, tomorrow, next week) or a scrubber: minutes, then hours, then days.

items.title: With a reason
items.body: Waiting for someone, no time now, needs focus, not urgent, not feeling it. Each picks a return time; waiting can come back “until there’s news”.

items.title: Insights
items.body: Loops (snoozed three times), pile-ups on the same morning, items on the same topic, items gone quiet. One insight at a time, never a report.

items.title: Notifications with buttons
items.body: New review requests, mentions, approvals, failed checks, due reminders. Done or Snooze without opening Remora. Hide the message text per tool, for screen shares.

groups.name: Reviews
groups.intro: Less context switching between your tools.

items.title: Review prep
items.body: An estimate and what the change touches (migrations, auth, infrastructure, dependencies), from file paths and line counts only. Code is never stored.

items.title: Review sessions
items.body: Start session goes through your review requests one by one, quick wins first: ⏎ open, D done, S snooze, → skip.

items.title: Links between tools
items.body: A pull request and a Linear issue with a similar title are shown together, even when nobody linked them.

items.title: Waiting assistant
items.body: Suggested reviewers when there are none, a drafted nudge when they stay silent. Written locally; you copy it, Remora never sends.

groups.name: Assistant (optional)
groups.intro: Off by default. Only where your organization allows external AI.

items.title: Brief
items.body: Three sentences and the items to handle first, with Claude Code on your plan, the Claude API or an OpenAI-compatible model. Cached, so it doesn’t spend tokens on every open.

items.title: Bundle summaries
items.body: Two sentences on a busy bundle, with a lighter model. Reused while the bundle holds the same items.

items.title: Triage
items.body: For a crowded Snoozed tab: keep, reschedule, let go or do now, item by item. You confirm every change.

privacy.enforce_title: Checked in code, covered by tests.

enforce.title: Declared destinations
enforce.body: Every plugin declares the hosts it may reach. A test fails if one doesn’t.

enforce.title: One gate
enforce.body: Plugins only get a network client limited to their own hosts. Anything else fails with “Blocked: not an allowed destination”, look-alike domains included.

enforce.title: External AI off by default
enforce.body: Assistant plugins are refused until external AI is allowed, except a server on your computer; then the brief, summaries and triage appear.

enforce.title: On-device intelligence
enforce.body: Sorting messages, topic similarity, ranking and snooze advice run on your computer: with Apple’s on-device language models on the Mac, with keyword rules on Windows. Nothing is sent.

enforce.title: No telemetry
enforce.body: No analytics, no crash reporting, no update check unless you turn updates on. Fonts and logos are bundled, never downloaded.

enforce.title: Erase local data
enforce.body: Settings → Privacy lists every connected account’s destinations, and erases everything Remora stored in one click.

privacy.mdm_lead: Deploy a configuration profile for the preference domain fr.igitscor.remora. Settings → Privacy then shows “Managed by your organization”, and users can’t change it.
privacy.windows: The Windows app follows the same model: Credential Manager for tokens, %LOCALAPPDATA%\fr.igitscor.remora for data, and the policy under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Remora (Group Policy or Intune). For a fleet, Remora.msi installs it for every user, as the deployment guide explains.
